# Rookery

> Rookery is a free, open-source (MIT) SSH client and server manager for Windows 10 / 11 and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel). One tab per server with its terminal, SFTP files, a safe remote file editor, Docker, logs, services, processes and databases. Everything is stored encrypted on the user's own computer: no account, no cloud, no tracking.

- Website: https://aagzamov-dev.github.io/Rookery/
- Source code: https://github.com/aagzamov-dev/Rookery
- Downloads: https://github.com/aagzamov-dev/Rookery/releases/latest
- Changelog: https://github.com/aagzamov-dev/Rookery/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG.md

## What it does

- Terminal: fast SSH terminal with tabs, snippets with variables, search, session logs and highlighted ERROR / WARN lines.
- Files: SFTP browser with drag and drop that can follow the terminal's current folder.
- Editor: edit remote text files (.env, YAML, nginx, JSON, code) with highlighting, formatting and problem checks. Saving checks the file was not changed by someone else (SHA-256); if it was, a three-way merge is shown instead of overwriting. A backup of the previous version is kept locally. Can save with sudo.
- Docker: containers grouped by compose project, live CPU and memory, logs, start / stop / restart, shell.
- Databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB through the server's SSH session or directly. Tables open like HeidiSQL (data, filters, sorting, structure, foreign keys). Production connections are read-only until changes are allowed and committed.
- Dashboard: all servers at a glance (CPU, RAM, disk, containers) with a needs-attention list.
- Import servers from MobaXterm, PuTTY and ~/.ssh/config.
- Backup and sync between your computers through an encrypted file in a folder you choose (for example Google Drive or Dropbox).

## Security

- Passwords, keys and tokens are kept in a local vault encrypted with the user's master password.
- Rookery only connects to the user's own servers.
- Updates are signed and verified before they install.

## Install

- Windows: download Rookery_x.y.z_x64-setup.exe from the latest release and run it (no admin rights). SmartScreen may warn because the app is not code-signed yet: More info → Run anyway.
- macOS: download Rookery_x.y.z_universal.dmg, drag Rookery to Applications, then run once in Terminal:
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Rookery.app"
  This is needed because Rookery is not signed with a paid Apple Developer account yet, so macOS reports it as "damaged". The command only removes the "downloaded from the internet" mark from Rookery.
- After installing, Rookery updates itself.

## Not available yet

- Linux, Android and iOS versions.
